text:
maria: Heads-up — observed 5 OOMs on prod replicas in the chat-long-context fleet (requests with ~12k-16k tokens) from 03:22–03:35 UTC. Pattern: KV cache grows past slab thresholds during steady long convo, followed by a kernel selector thrash (switching between fast_fp16 and int8-fallback) and then allocator OOM.

devon: Can you paste the allocator traces + kernel-selection logs?

maria: Pasted snippets below. note: timestamps are from the same host.
```
[03:24:11] serving/runtime: alloc failed: slab=evictable_pool size=48MB reason=fragmentation
[03:24:11] kvcache: shard(7) entries=248k prefixes=190k kv_bytes=3.6GB reuse_hits=2.1k
[03:24:11] kernel-selector: choose(int8-optimized) -> try(fast_fp16) fallback=int8-emswitch
[03:24:11] runtime: OOM: allocator.cpp:487 cannot reserve contiguous 64MB
```

maria: Also saw repeated small kernel switches logged every 100-200ms which lines up with batch-arrival jitter. Looks like selector keeps oscillating when memory headroom is tight.

jia: That's the classic kernel-thrashing + cache-growth combo. When the selector toggles kernels it temporarily increases memory due to different workspace+KV layout and the kvcache doesn't immediately shrink.

andre: Do we have telemetry for per-kernel working set sizes (ws) + slabmap snapshots over time for one of these repros? If so we can see which kernel pair causes the peak.

maria: Uploading short profile to S3 (s3://redwood-prod-profiles/1758883333/). Key points from the profile: peak resident jumped 1.1GB right after switching to fast_fp16, and the kvcache didn't evict because eviction score was below threshold (reuse_score high).

devon: Could be our eviction heuristic relying too much on reuse_score. Long contexts keep high reuse even when the reuse is for very old prefixes that won't be needed dynamically. Suggest adding an age-decay multiplier to reuse_score when global headroom < X.

jia: Agreed. Also we should consider a quick soft-shedding policy: when memory headroom < 200MB and kernel selector requests a bigger workspace, proactively trim KV prefixes with low recent access, and reduce batch-window for a short period to avoid selector flip-flops.

andre: For immediate mitigation in prod, can we push a thin runtime patch: 1) bias kernel selector toward lower-ws kernels when free_mem < 300MB; 2) make eviction proactively drop prefixes with last_access > 15m if their next_token_prob < threshold.

maria: I can build a runtime patch but prefer not to change eviction algos mid-day without kill-switch. Plan: ship selector bias + an emergency runtime flag to enable aggressive trimming. Deploy to canary first.

devon: Also add a request-level fallback: if kernel switch would increase ws and we see imminent OOM, fall back to CPU path for that request (with throttled concurrency) rather than fail. CPU path is slower but keeps SLA for p99 latency? Might be acceptable for very long contexts.

jia: CPU fallback needs circuit-breaker. We should only allow <5% of concurrent requests to move to CPU fallback to avoid blowing up cloud infra.

maria: For the reproducible test we ran locally I added a temporary flag: 
```
--runtime.kernel_bias=prefer_low_ws_if_free<400MB
--kvcache.trim_age=900s
--kvcache.trim_mode=soft
```
Result: peak resident dropped ~900MB and kernel-selector stopped switching for the duration of the test. No functional regressions observed.

andre: Good. Action items:
- maria: open a short-lived PR for selector-bias + runtime flag (canary-only by default).
- devon: prototype age-decay on reuse_score and a soft-evict policy; test on replay harness.
- jia: add CPU-fallback circuit-breaker and throttling metric + alert.
- ops: schedule a canary rollout and monitor p95/p99 + OOM counter.

devon: One more note — batching heuristics: our current batch-window=8ms can exacerbate kernel churn when request arrival jitter moves it across workspace boundaries. We might benefit from adaptive batch-window that increases slightly under memory pressure to stabilize kernel choice.

maria: Put a small experiment in the PR: when free_mem < 500MB, batch-window -> min(batch-window * 1.5, 20ms). That stabilized the selector in the local run.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1183 (linked to recent OOMs). Notifying on-call.

andre: Expected rollout timeline?

maria: I can get the PR up in the next 2 hours for canary. Will include runbook steps to flip the emergency flag off.

devon: For long-term: add per-prefix importance scoring (recent_hits / token_distance) and integrate into eviction. That should avoid dropping highly reused short prefixes while shedding long unused prefixes from historical context.

jia: Also add a micro-benchmark for kernel-switch cost (memory delta + time) so selector can reason with a numeric cost model rather than heuristics.

maria: TL;DR: immediate mitigation = selector bias + soft trim flag + canary rollout. Medium-term = age-decay reuse scoring, CPU-fallback circuit, adaptive batching and kernel cost model.

andre: 👍 Please paste PR link when ready and tag me + oncall.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4021 (draft). Canary job queued. Will post results in this thread.

devon: Thanks — when canary looks good, we should run a 30m soak on ~10% of prod replicas before wider rollout.

maria: ack. will coordinate with ops.

sre-bot: Canary deployment started for pr/4021 -> fleet: chat-long-context-canary (10% nodes). Job id: canary-1758884001

maria: will follow up with perf numbers once canary finishes.

(End of thread)
